walkthroughs.body_html:
Theory & Methods — a core area of GCSE Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Theory & Methods brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Theory & Methods.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

options: Anomie
Verstehen
Praxis
Alienation

mcqs.q: Which research method involves in-depth participant observation?
options: Survey
Experiment
Ethnography
Content analysis
Snowball sampling is a type of random sampling.

When studying hard-to-reach or hidden populations (drug users, undocumented migrants) where a sampling frame doesn't exist — participants recruit further participants. It sacrifices representativeness for access.
Snowball sampling is only used in winter research.
A self-fulfilling prophecy is when teachers predict the future accurately.
The unspoken norms, values, and behaviours taught implicitly in schools.
Topics removed from the syllabus.
Secret lessons teachers deliberately hide from students.
A self-fulfilling prophecy is when teachers predict the future accurately.

mcqs.q: What is a self-fulfilling prophecy in education?
options: A self-fulfilling prophecy is when teachers predict the future accurately.
A self-fulfilling prophecy is when a student predicts their own grade correctly.

When teachers' expectations (often based on labels) influence pupil behaviour and achievement — pupils labelled as 'bright' tend to do better, those labelled 'thick' worse, regardless of underlying ability (Rosenthal and Jacobson).
